newsitem.title: CANADA: World Wide Minerals proposes merger.
newsitem.headline: World Wide Minerals proposes merger.

text.p: World Wide Minerals Ltd said on Monday it planned to merge with Kazakstan Goldfields Corp.
The successor company would be called World Wide Minerals Ltd and would continue to trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange, the companies said.
Kazakstan Goldfields is reactivating three gold mines in Kazakhstan. World Wide mines uranium in that country.

World Wide said it agreed to acquire from Central Asia Goldfields the seven million common shares or 22 percent interest held by that company in Kazakstan Goldfields for 6.7 million World Wide common shares.

World Wide also agreed to purchase from Central Asia Goldfields its 25 percent carried interest in Gold Pool, of which Kazakstan Goldfields owns 75 percent. World Wide would pay 4.75 million common shares.
World Wide has 51.1 million shares outstanding. The transactions would mean 35.2 million shares issued by World Wide.
The proposals were approved by the boards of all three companies and would be submitted to shareholders for approval to be effective by the end of February 1997, the companies said.
